html:
The Japanese warlord who completed the unification of Japan and founded the Tokugawa shogunate, which ruled a peaceful, mostly closed country from Edo for over 250 years.

He spent part of his childhood as a hostage of rival clans. He became the ally of Oda Nobunaga, then a leading vassal of Toyotomi Hideyoshi, who moved him to the Kanto plain in the east. There he built up the small castle town of Edo, today's Tokyo.

After Hideyoshi died, Ieyasu won the battle of Sekigahara in 1600 against the lords loyal to Hideyoshi's young son. In 1603 the emperor named him shogun. Two years later he passed the title to his son but kept real power. In 1614 and 1615 he besieged Osaka Castle and destroyed the Toyotomi family.

He set the pattern of Tokugawa Japan: lords bound by strict rules, a fixed class order, the great roads such as the Tōkaidō, and growing control of foreign trade and Christianity. He died in 1616 and is honoured at the shrine of Nikkō Tōshō-gū. His line ruled until 1867.
sum: The Japanese warlord who completed the unification of Japan and founded the Tokugawa shogunate, which ruled a peaceful, mostly closed country from Edo for over 250 years.
